I am primarily an acoustic guy. I've noticed that my posture is terrible, as the body size of the guitar makes me kind of hunch around it. I went to a concert the other night and noticed their (acoustic) guitar player had the same posture happening. As I play and gig fairly regularly, it's starting to cause some serious back pain. I've had my back cramp up in the middle of a set and have to power through it. I was thinking of trying out an electric acoustic for the smaller body size, but I didn't like the acoustic tone of the Taylor T-5. Has anyone tried the Godin? Any other suggestions?

If you play right-handed and play seated, don't place the guitar on your right thigh. This position forces you to angle your right arm and shoulder back into an unnatural position in order to reach around the guitar and can lead to chronic pain.

Instead, place the body of the guitar between your legs, much like a seated banjo player or classical guitar player. This permits a far more natural position and will eliminate back and shoulder pain. Be patient, it may take a few weeks or months, but it will yield results. I've been playing dreadnoughts for 15 years and switched after a few years because I had terrible shoulder pain.

What about standing? I've been trying (unsuccessfully) to find a good ergonomic position by standing with a straight posture where my back is comfortable and trying to put the guitar in a position that alters that the least.

I'm afraid I'm a little clueless on issues related to standing. I play lower, more like a rock player (sound hole around one's belly button). Bluegrass players often play with the guitar a little higher (bottom of sound hole on one's belly button). I think this is partly fashion, partly tradition. Unaware back issues are a cause or result. Unless the guitar is heavy like a Les Paul, I just don't think it should be giving you back issues. Maybe it's exacerbating an existing issue like degenerative disk disease?

Oh, there's definitely some long term injury damage there, just trying to mitigate it as best as possible. My electric is heavy as all get out, but I can stand with that pretty easily due to the thin body. I've also started turning the guitar slightly to the right, as I found that if I am standing perfectly straight, it forces my left shoulder back into an odd position.
